open_loop: The 92nd minute in Madrid: 10-man England lead 3-2, and Trafford makes two saves in about two seconds to finish Spain's 43-match unbeaten run. How did City's 'cup goalkeeper' end up there?
hook_suggestion: Man City paid £31m to bring him home. Then benched him.
hook_alt: Spain again. Stoppage time again. Trafford again.

beats.fact: Spain 2-3 England, Nations League, Riyadh Air Metropolitano, Madrid. England led 3-0, then Elliot Anderson was sent off in the 63rd minute and Spain scored twice. With England down to 10 men, Trafford made a double save in the 92nd minute to protect the 3-2 win, which ended Spain's 43-match unbeaten run.
beats.note: Don't name the players the double save denied. Sky says Fermín López then Oyarzabal, BBC says Yamal/Fermín López, and ESPN names nobody. Outlets disagree, so name none.

beats.fact: CHAPTER 1: Trafford spent almost eight years in Manchester City's academy. In 2023 he saved a stoppage-time penalty in the European Under-21 Championship final against Spain, England kept six consecutive clean sheets in the tournament, and City sold him to Burnley in a deal worth up to £19m.

CHAPTER 2: In 2025 City bought him back from Burnley for £31m. City's own site confirmed a five-year deal and called it an emotional return. Then City signed Gianluigi Donnarumma and Trafford was reduced to Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

He left City for Leeds for £45m in summer 2026 and became their No 1. BBC says he has now been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee twice. He then started in Madrid ahead of Jordan Pickford, and Thomas Tuchel singled out the double save.
beats.quote: The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.

beats.fact: Trafford, 24, has 5 England caps, all in 2026. Pickford, 32, has 94 and has been first choice for almost a decade. After the game Tuchel said there's no No 1.
